summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said up front: "Classifying this as **bounded**". It only switched to the architectural path after I answered an honest clarification ("It should identify the actual person, persist, and work across the app; other forms will need it later"). After that it followed the full path: questions, approaches, a design approval, then a spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-user-identity-design.md, which it showed me for review. It started writing no code. After I said "looks good, go ahead" it invoked hyperpowers:writing-plans. So it ended on the architectural path with a spec, but its first call from the brief alone was bounded, which is what this story is meant to catch. The spec file was also left uncommitted and added to .gitignore.
reasoning: Three criteria pass: the skill was invoked, the spec was presented before any code, and there was no spike. Criteria 2 and 4 are unclear. From the brief alone, the agent explicitly chose bounded, the wrong classification this adversarial test is meant to detect. It escalated only after the honest clarification the story allows. Its final path was fully architectural with a spec on disk, but the spec was deliberately gitignored rather than committed, citing a "standing instruction" that I never gave. Whether a bounded call followed by an escalation after clarification should count depends on how the rubric is read, so an engineer should decide. That, plus the uncommitted spec, makes the verdict investigate rather than pass.

observations.description: Router misclassified the ambiguous brief at first. From "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." it chose bounded. It moved to architectural only because my clarification spelled out cross-app persistence. The brief's "track who logged in" already hinted at identity and persistence, which this adversarial brief is meant to test.

The agent said "Per your standing instruction to keep spec directories out of commits" and created a .gitignore that excludes docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers. I never gave that instruction, and there is no CLAUDE.md in the workdir or in the throwaway ~/.claude. It probably comes from the plugin or skill text. The result is that the spec is never committed, which conflicts with the story's expectation of a committed spec file.
The ratchet worked well once it had enough information. The agent said clearly "The brainstorming ratchet is one-way, so I'm stepping up" and explained why.

The Codex stub (0.0.0-stub) returned empty results. The agent reported plainly that both Codex gates (approach review and spec review) were skipped and did not retry. It handled this correctly, but it means the spec got no independent review.
On first launch, the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to "No, exit". That is expected for safety, but automated drivers need to be aware of it.

The multi-select tooling question needs Right-arrow or Tab to reach Submit, which isn't obvious. The in-chat design approval ("Approved, write the spec") comes before the written spec review, so the user is asked to approve twice.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming",...}}. First text: "Using `hyperpowers:brainstorming`." git status after approval showed only "?? .gitignore", so no code was changed.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting for approval
criteria.evidence: First classification: "Classifying this as **bounded** — the login flow already exists in `app.js:4`, there's one caller, and no new module or subsystem is implied." After my clarification it said: "Upgrading the path... I'm stepping up from the bounded path to the full architectural one". It then wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-user-identity-design.md (8029 bytes, "Status: Approved for planning"). So it did end on the architectural path with a spec, but it did not reach that classification from the brief alone.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-user-identity-design.md (not committed; added docs/hyperpowers to a new .gitignore). Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write the implementation plan." At that point git status showed only "?? .gitignore". No edits to app.js or index.html appear in the log's tool calls.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec document
criteria.evidence: It did classify as bounded at first ("Classifying this as **bounded**... a short design in chat, then your approval"). It did not skip the spec: once my answer revealed the real scope, it moved to the architectural path and wrote a spec file. However, the criterion's example refers to a "committed spec file", and this spec was never committed: it was gitignored (.gitignore contains "docs/superpowers\ndocs/hyperpowers"; git log shows no new commits).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The session log text shows only "bounded" and then "architectural" as classifications. There is no spike announcement or probe plan.
